title: Patient, visit and revenue distribution across the four hospitals
numerical_observation: Largest site HSP-01 has 52,684 visits (33.2% of network) and 752.6 visits per bed; smallest site HSP-04 has 26,183 visits.
pattern_identified: Volume concentration is uneven: the two central sites carry disproportionate OPD load.
business_implication: Site-level capacity planning must differ; a single network-wide staffing ratio would starve the busiest site.

title: Outpatient versus inpatient volume and revenue
numerical_observation: 31,282 admissions vs 158,744 OPD visits (16.5% of events) yet IPD generates 92.3% of billing value.
pattern_identified: Classic 5/95 volume-to-value inversion typical of Indian community hospitals.
business_implication: Inpatient capacity and case-mix management drive financial sustainability; OPD drives reach and gate-keeping.

title: Monthly OPD volume with trend line
numerical_observation: Monthly volume ranges 2,967-8,508 (CV 24.37%), trend +384 visits/year; last-12-month average 2141.1% above the first 12 months.
pattern_identified: Secular growth on top of a repeating seasonal cycle, not a flat demand curve.
business_implication: Capacity must be planned with a growth buffer; a static staffing model will progressively under-serve the network.

title: Quarterly OPD volume
numerical_observation: Peak quarter 2024Q4 (16,872); trough 2022Q2 (9,626).
pattern_identified: Q3 (Jul-Sep) is consistently the softest quarter, Q4 the strongest.
business_implication: Elective camps, screening drives and elective surgery scheduling should be loaded into Q3 slack.

title: Patient volume and billing value by age band
numerical_observation: Patients aged 45+ are 44.5% of the base but contribute 72.8% of billing value; the 15-29 band is the single largest volume band (18.7%).
pattern_identified: Value is age-skewed: the 45+ cohort generates revenue far ahead of its headcount.
business_implication: Chronic-disease programmes (diabetes, hypertension, cardiac) have the highest value density per enrolled patient.

title: Gender distribution and mean billing
numerical_observation: Female 21,627 (51.7%), male 20,207 (48.3%); mean billing M INR 40,342 vs F INR 41,642.
pattern_identified: Gender mix is near-balanced but male patients carry higher average value.
business_implication: Maternity and paediatric bundles are volume anchors rather than value anchors - price and capacity them accordingly.

title: Department utilisation and revenue intensity
numerical_observation: Top three departments (General Medicine, Pulmonology, Orthopaedics) absorb 50.0% of OPD visits; revenue per visit ranges INR 688 (Ophthalmology) to INR 61,462 (General Surgery).
pattern_identified: Volume is concentrated in generalist departments while value concentrates in specialist ones.
business_implication: Queue redesign should target generalist OPD; specialist slots should be protected and scheduled, not queued.

title: Diagnosis mix after canonicalisation
numerical_observation: 45 canonical diagnoses after mapping; top diagnosis Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus = 12,927 visits (8.1%); chronic conditions account for 62.5% of all OPD visits.
pattern_identified: Chronic disease dominates demand, not acute episodic care.
business_implication: A chronic-care programme is the highest-leverage clinical intervention available to the network.

title: Billing line amount distribution before and after log transform
numerical_observation: 263,073 lines totalling INR 171.74 crore; median INR 715 vs mean INR 6,528; skew 6.4, kurtosis 68.1. The top 10% of lines carry 72.6% of value.
pattern_identified: Extreme right skew with a small number of high-value inpatient lines.
business_implication: Log transform is mandatory before distance-based clustering; raw rupees would let a single admission dominate the geometry.

title: Revenue contribution by hospital and service line
numerical_observation: HSP-01 contributes INR 63.88 crore of INR 171.74 crore (37.2%); IPD room charges alone are 57.2% of value.
pattern_identified: Revenue is dominated by inpatient room charges, with a stable second tier of procedures.
business_implication: Bed utilisation and ALOS control are the two biggest revenue levers in the network.

title: Distribution of visits per patient
numerical_observation: Mean 3.79 visits, median 1; 52.2% of patients have exactly one visit, P90 = 9, max = 58.
pattern_identified: A one-and-done majority alongside a small but important high-frequency tail.
business_implication: Retention, not acquisition, is the constraint: converting single-visit patients into a second visit is the cheapest growth available.

title: Distribution of patient recency
numerical_observation: Median recency 202 days; 37.0% of patients have not been seen for over a year; 8.7% visited in the last 30 days.
pattern_identified: The panel is bimodal: an active core and a large dormant population.
business_implication: Reactivation of the dormant tier is a defined, addressable revenue pool with no acquisition cost.

title: Length-of-stay distribution and department comparison
numerical_observation: ALOS 5.29 days (median 4); P90 9 days; longest department Cardiology at 7.1 days.
pattern_identified: Right-skewed LOS with a specialist-department tail.
business_implication: A 0.5-day ALOS reduction on the longest-stay department releases meaningful bed capacity without reducing care quality.

title: Missing-value profile across raw tables
numerical_observation: Highest raw missingness is visit_id::lab_tests at 6.00%; arriving as 10 table-column cells.
pattern_identified: Missingness is low and structurally random except for lab-to-visit linkage.
business_implication: Imputation is defensible and does not need to be aggressive; the lab linkage gap is an integration problem, not a data-entry problem.

title: Spearman correlation among engineered features
numerical_observation: Frequency-monetary rho 0.70; recency-frequency rho -0.40; admission-bed-days rho 0.81.
pattern_identified: Frequency and monetary are positively but not redundantly correlated, so both carry independent signal.
business_implication: Keeping F and M as separate axes is justified, but the K-means feature set must drop near-duplicate columns to avoid double weighting.

title: IQR outlier detection on key utilisation features
numerical_observation: Outlier counts at the 1.5xIQR fence: frequency 2,811 (6.72%); monetary 6,491 (15.52%); avg_billing_per_visit 7,268 (17.37%); total_bed_days 1,431 (3.42%); lab_count 2,565 (6.13%).
pattern_identified: Quantile scoring and log-scaling are required; these are genuine heavy users, not errors.
business_implication: High-utilisation and high-complexity patients are retained and profiled as a segment - never deleted.

title: Seasonal index of OPD demand
numerical_observation: Peak Jan at index 139, trough Jun at 79 - an amplitude of 60 index points (60% swing).
pattern_identified: Winter months are consistently over-indexed; monsoon months under-index.
business_implication: Roster flex of roughly +/-15% around the annual mean is needed; hiring to the annual average would misallocate staff for 8 months of 12.

title: K-means model selection: elbow, silhouette and bootstrap stability
numerical_observation: Silhouette peaks at k=2 (score 0.648); inertia's largest marginal drop is at k=4. Bootstrap ARI by k: k=2:1.00, k=3:1.00, k=4:0.99, k=5:1.00, k=6:0.99, k=7:0.99, k=8:0.88, k=9:0.94, k=10:0.94.
pattern_identified: Absolute silhouette values are low because behavioural data is continuous without separated blobs; the decision must therefore rest on stability and interpretability as well as separation.
business_implication: k is chosen where silhouette is competitive, ARI stability is high, every segment clears the 5% size floor, and the segments map onto actionable care pathways.

title: PCA projection of K-means clusters
numerical_observation: PC1+PC2 retain 86.5% of variance; cluster sizes range 5,971 to 22,611 patients (smallest = 14.3% of base).
pattern_identified: Clusters form a graded continuum rather than tight isolated islands - normal for behavioural segmentation.
business_implication: Low separation is acceptable when segments differ materially on the KPIs that drive operational decisions; the profile table is what must be validated, not the scatter plot.

title: Feature-level comparison of K-means segments
numerical_observation: Segment-level means for the seven profiling KPIs; ranges: recency 183-470 days, frequency 1.5-8.3 visits, monetary INR 2,354-165,984.
pattern_identified: Segments differ by multiples, not percentages, on the core KPIs.
business_implication: Each segment therefore needs a different operating model rather than a different message.

title: RFM segment sizes and shares
numerical_observation: 7 rule-based segments; largest Hibernating 13,650 (32.6%), smallest High-Value Dormant 1,172 (2.8%).
pattern_identified: Rule-based scoring produces a small 'Champions' core and a large residual.
business_implication: The residual 'Hibernating' tier is too large to be operationally actionable on its own - this is the structural weakness of the RFM approach for this population.

title: Segment migration and retention between two independent 18-month periods
numerical_observation: ARI between the two independent segmentations for the 16,536 patients active in both periods is 0.158. Retention ranges 8.9% to 92.1%; off-diagonal migration is 50.0% of the cohort.
pattern_identified: The high-value segment is far stickier than the dormant segment, which behaves as a revolving door.
business_implication: Retention investment should be concentrated on the engaged segment where status is defensible; the dormant segment needs a reactivation programme with a short payback horizon, not a loyalty programme.

title: Segment size drift between the two periods
numerical_observation: Dormant One-Time: 6,732 -> 2,170 (-67.8%); Frequent OPD Regulars: 7,913 -> 13,814 (+74.6%); High-Acuity Inpatient: 1,891 -> 552 (-70.8%).
pattern_identified: Growth is not uniform: the engaged segment compounds while the dormant pool also grows as one-visit patients accumulate.
business_implication: Left unmanaged, the dormant pool becomes the dominant cost of the panel; the reactivation programme in the recommendations targets exactly this drift.

title: Cost-benefit analysis and sensitivity of the four recommendations
numerical_observation: Total implementation cost INR 62.7 lakh against projected annual benefit INR 333.9 lakh; portfolio ROI 433%. Individual ROI ranges 23% to 688%.
pattern_identified: All four business cases are positive in the base case; the readmission-prevention case is the largest single contributor and the reactivation case is the most assumption-sensitive.
business_implication: Fund in the order of benefit-to-cost ratio, stage-gate the reactivation programme on wave-1 results, and re-validate every assumption against the pilot cohort before full commitment.

title: Model comparison and KPI separation of the final segments
numerical_observation: 7 of 10 criteria favour K-means, 2 favour RFM. 8 of 9 KPIs exceed the 0.30 materiality floor; the widest is avg_adm_rate at 2.73.
pattern_identified: K-means wins on the criteria that determine whether a segmentation can be operated; RFM wins on transparency and reproducibility only.
business_implication: K-means is the primary segmentation; RFM is retained as a secondary screening tool for the OPD front desk because its per-patient score is immediate.
